toegepas.voor: 'n wasbak en 'n watertenk op die werf
toegepas.na: 'n wasbak en op die werf 'n watertenk
toegepas.rede_vinder: As written, 'op die werf' seems to apply to the bath, bucket and basin too; moving it makes it apply only to the tank.
toegepas.fout: 'op die werf' at the end of the list reads as if the bath, bucket and basin are also on the yard.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Moving the phrase in front of 'n watertenk' ties it to the tank only, adds nothing, and reads naturally.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017 writes 'ná' (after) with an acute accent to tell it apart from 'na' (to).
toegepas.fout: 'na' meaning 'after' is written without the AWS acute accent.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A plain spelling fix that tells 'after' apart from 'to'; the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.na: Hy val vooroor in die water en
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'val vooroor' is the idiomatic Afrikaans for falling forward, and 'val ... in' with no object sounds unfinished.
toegepas.fout: 'val vorentoe in' with no object sounds unfinished and wooden.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'val vooroor in die water' is the idiomatic expression and only names the water the paragraph is already about.

toegepas.voor: is dit vol mense en die rand
toegepas.na: is dit vol mense, en die rand
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017 puts a comma before 'en' here because it joins two sentences, each with its own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have a subject and verb ('dit is' / 'die rand is').

toegepas.voor: ongelyk en glad en hy kan
toegepas.na: ongelyk en glad, en hy kan
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017 comma: 'hy kan skielik wegval' is a second sentence with its own subject and verb; without the comma the sentence also has two 'en's in a row.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' introducing a clause with its own subject and verb ('hy kan ... wegval').
toegepas.rede_keurder: Correct AWS 2017 comma; the first 'en' stays without one because it sits inside a list of adjectives.

toegepas.rede_vinder: A Grade 4 child may read 'goeie reën' (heavy rain) as 'good rain'; 'swaar reën' is clear, and 'ná' takes the AWS accent; 'gewoonlik' is not touched.
toegepas.fout: 'goeie reën' can read as 'good rain' to a Grade 4 child, and 'na' (after) is missing its AWS accent.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Ná swaar reën' is plain and clear, keeps the meaning, and leaves the protected 'gewoonlik' alone.

toegepas.blok: Die reëls wat jou veilig hou
toegepas.voor: Swem nooit alleen nie en net waar
toegepas.na: Swem nooit alleen nie en swem net waar
toegepas.rede_vinder: After 'nooit ... nie', the second half needs its own verb, or it reads as if 'nooit' also covers 'net waar'.
toegepas.fout: Without its own verb the second half can read as falling under 'nooit', which would turn the rule upside down.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Repeating 'swem' removes a dangerous ambiguity without changing what the rule tells the child to do.

toegepas.blok: Die reëls wat jou veilig hou
toegepas.na: waar die badmeester jou kan sien
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'sien' needs an object here, as in the first rule ('waar 'n grootmens jou kan sien').
toegepas.fout: 'sien' is left without the object the sentence needs.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Adding 'jou' completes the grammar and matches the first rule; the instruction is unchanged.

laat_vaar.voor: kan in water verdrink wat nie tot by sy knieë kom nie
laat_vaar.na: kan verdrink in water wat nie tot by sy knieë kom nie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Putting the relative clause straight after 'water' makes the sentence easier for a Grade 4 reader to follow.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'kan in water verdrink wat ...' is ordinary Afrikaans word order and reads clearly, so the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The bank of a river or dam is a 'wal' in Afrikaans; 'kant' in the plural is vague here.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The paragraph uses 'kant' consistently for the edge, 'walle' of a dam could be read as the dam wall, and the original reads fine.

laat_vaar.blok: Hoe dit werklik lyk as iemand sukkel
laat_vaar.voor: In flieks swaai en skreeu die mens wat verdrink.
laat_vaar.na: In flieks skreeu die mens wat verdrink en swaai hy sy arms.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'swaai' with no object sounds unfinished; the arms are what the verb means, so no content is added.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The original is crisp, and the proposal is longer and invites a misreading of 'wat verdrink en swaai' as one relative clause.

laat_vaar.blok: Die reëls wat jou veilig hou
laat_vaar.voor: Loop by die rand en moenie
laat_vaar.na: Stap by die rand en moenie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Stap' makes the contrast with 'hardloop' plain; 'loop by die rand' can also be read as 'go to the edge'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Loop' against 'hardloop' is already the natural Afrikaans contrast, so the swap is a lateral move inside a safety rule.

laat_vaar.blok: As iemand in die moeilikheid is
laat_vaar.voor: Dit is die eerste ding en die belangrikste ding.
laat_vaar.na: Dit is die eerste en die belangrikste ding.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Repeating 'ding' is wooden; the emphasis stays the same without it.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The repeated 'ding' is deliberate emphasis on the first safety action, and removing it weakens that emphasis.

na_skrywer.voor: kan sy kop of sy nek breek
na_skrywer.na: kan sy kop beseer of sy nek breek
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'sy kop breek' is not natural Afrikaans for a head injury, and it also reads like the idiom 'kop breek oor' (to puzzle over something); 'nek breek' stays.
na_skrywer.fout: 'sy kop breek' is not natural Afrikaans for a head injury.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but 'beseer' weakens a hazard statement from 'break' to 'injure', so the writer needs to find another fix.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.blok: Die reëls wat jou veilig hou
na_skrywer.voor: nie op sy foon werk nie
na_skrywer.na: nie met sy foon besig wees nie
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'op sy foon werk' is a calque of 'work on his phone'; 'met sy foon besig wees' is idiomatic and covers any use of the phone, which is what the rule means.
na_skrywer.fout: 'op sy foon werk' is a calque of English 'work on his phone'.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but the proposal widens what the safety rule forbids, so the writer owns that change.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.blok: Die reëls wat jou veilig hou
na_skrywer.voor: Hou die hek van 'n swembad se heining toe
na_skrywer.na: Hou die hek in die heining om 'n swembad toe
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The stacked possessive 'die hek van 'n swembad se heining' is heavy going for a Grade 4 reader.
na_skrywer.fout: The stacked possessive 'die hek van 'n swembad se heining' is heavy going for a Grade 4 reader.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The awkwardness is real, but the proposal restructures a safety instruction and is not clearly easier, so the writer should fix it.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.blok: As iemand in die moeilikheid is
na_skrywer.voor: Gee 'n stok aan of gooi iets wat dryf naby hom.
na_skrywer.na: Hou 'n stok na die persoon uit of gooi naby hom iets wat dryf.
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'Gee aan' has no receiver, and 'hom' is far from the person it refers to (the closest noun is 'een'); the word order also makes it unclear what 'naby hom' attaches to. The action (reach or throw from the bank) is unchanged.
na_skrywer.fout: 'Gee aan' has no receiver, and 'hom' sits closest to 'een' rather than to the person in trouble.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but the proposal changes the rescue action from handing to holding out, which is safety wording the writer owns.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Stoei en indruk verander 'n speletjie gou in 'n ongeluk.
vlae.rede: 'indruk' can mean pushing someone into the water or holding someone under, and as a noun it also means 'impression'; the right wording ('mekaar instoot' or 'mekaar onderdruk') cannot be chosen without guessing which is meant.
The block heading 'werk anders' (work differently) is slightly unnatural for places ('is anders' would be more usual); a heading is not proposed as a change, so this is left to the writer.
